relations.note: Some genealogies name Esarg as Dían Cécht’s father.
A disputed genealogical parsing makes Échtach Esarg his father.
Some later place-lore makes the Dagda Dían Cécht’s father.
Genealogical arrangements make Goibniu his brother or craft-relative.
Genealogical arrangements make Crédne his brother or craft-relative.
Genealogical arrangements make Luchta his brother or craft-relative.
Cú is recurrently named among Dían Cécht’s sons.
Cethen is recurrently named among Dían Cécht’s sons.
Cían is repeatedly identified as Dían Cécht’s son.
relations.source: Lebor Gabála Érenn; Cath Maige Tuired

relations.note: Míach is securely identified as Dían Cécht’s son.
relations.source: Lebor Gabála Érenn; Cath Maige Tuired

relations.note: Airmed is securely identified as Dían Cécht’s daughter.
relations.source: Lebor Gabála Érenn; Cath Maige Tuired

relations.note: Octriuil is identified as Dían Cécht’s son within the tale.
A genealogical tract names the poet Étan as his daughter.
Place-lore is interpreted as making Corand his son or protégé.
Dían Cécht is Lug’s grandfather through his son Cían.

relations.myth: Núadu receives the articulated silver hand
relations.note: Dían Cécht fits Núadu with a silver hand moving naturally.
First-battle traditions credit Dían Cécht with Núadu’s silver replacement.
relations.source: Cath Maige Tuired Cunga; Lebor Gabála

relations.myth: Dían Cécht kills his superior healer son
relations.note: After three healed wounds, Dían Cécht removes Míach’s brain.

relations.myth: Airmed sorts the herbs from Míach’s grave
relations.note: Dían Cécht mixes Airmed’s sorted herbs, obscuring their medicinal properties.

relations.myth: Physicians chant over the healing well Sláine
relations.note: Father and son jointly chant over Sláine during the battle.

relations.myth: Physicians chant over the healing well Sláine
relations.note: Míach joins Dían Cécht at Sláine despite his earlier narrated death.

relations.myth: Physicians chant over the healing well Sláine
relations.note: Airmed and Dían Cécht jointly operate the battlefield healing well.

relations.myth: Lug asks each specialist’s battle contribution
relations.note: Dían Cécht promises Lug next-day restoration of all nonfatal wounds.
Dían Cécht completely heals Midir’s eye without scar or blemish.
Mac Óc fetches Dían Cécht, who answers the summons.
Some accounts pair Dían Cécht’s medicine with Crédne’s craftsmanship.

relations.myth: Goibniu heals in the well Sláine
relations.note: Goibniu enters the physicians’ well wounded and emerges whole.
A euhemerizing recension says Dían Cécht and Goibniu died together.

relations.myth: The Fomoire bury the healing well
relations.note: Ochtríallach counters Dían Cécht’s healing work by ordering Sláine buried.
Dían Cécht kills and burns the poisonous serpent-being Méiche.

relations.myth: DanMachi medical rivalry and silver arm
relations.note: DanMachi reimagines Dian Cecht and Miach as rival medical gods.
